illustrations.visual_goal: Map six financial-foundation chapters into three connected stages, culminating in money and terms a company commitment can rely on.
illustrations.layout: Single stacked column on a tall 9:16 canvas, six chapter cards one per row, explanation lines nearly as large as the titles and wrapped onto short lines; Gemini's empty paper margins cropped by the driver so the lettering scales larger at phone width. Heading "UNDERSTAND". Stage label "Trace money and control": "Customers, lenders, investors" / "Customers pay for what they buy" / "Lenders must be repaid" / "Investors hope for a gain"; "Funding and control" / "Who receives money" / "and approves spending". Stage label "Interpret value and returns": "Valuation" / "Estimating what" / "a business is worth"; "Investor returns" / "Gains or losses" / "on invested money". Stage label "Confirm funding for the work": "Funding choices" / "Match the money" / "to the work"; "Cash flow" / "Money coming in" / "and going out". Teal arrows between cards; ochre banner "Know what can fund" / "a commitment to do the work".
illustrations.alt: Six chapters stacked in three stages. Trace money and control: Customers, lenders, investors (customers pay for what they buy, lenders must be repaid, investors hope for a gain) leads to Funding and control (who receives money and approves spending). Interpret value and returns: Valuation (estimating what a business is worth) leads to Investor returns (gains or losses on invested money). Confirm funding for the work: Funding choices (match the money to the work) leads to Cash flow (money coming in and going out). A final banner reads Know what can fund a commitment to do the work.
illustrations.caption: Six chapters in three stages, each linked below.
illustrations.aspect_ratio: 9:16 (Gemini canvas 768×1376), cropped to content with a 20-pixel paper margin
illustrations.placement: immediately after the heading The Learning Path, before the existing linked chapter walkthrough
illustrations.prompt:
Create ONE finished editorial framework illustration for the introduction to a part of OWNED: Product & Engineering Leadership Under Investors. It maps six chapters, their reading order and their shared purpose; it is not a business scene. Tall portrait 9:16 composition. Match the book's visual language: warm ivory paper, dark navy text, clean slightly organic ink outlines, pale muted teal cards, soft ochre highlights, restrained flat fills, extremely subtle paper texture.

LAYOUT, STRICT: a single vertical column. Every chapter card spans almost the full image width (side margins no wider than one twentieth of the image), one card per row, six rows in total, read top to bottom. Never place two cards side by side. The image will be shown on a narrow phone screen, so ALL lettering must be very large and the cards must fill the column with little empty space. Sizes: each card title is bold sans-serif with a cap height of about one fourteenth of the image width; each explanation line under a title is regular sans-serif at EXACTLY THE SAME SIZE as the title (only not bold), never smaller, so that the explanation lines are as tall as the title above them; the stage labels and the bottom banner use the title size. Reduce the gaps between cards and the arrows to the minimum, and shrink the top heading to the stage-label size, to make room for the large lettering. Explanations are broken onto the short lines given below, one line per line break, left-aligned next to the symbol, so no line is ever squeezed or shrunk to fit.

Heading at the top: "UNDERSTAND".

Stage label 1: "Trace money and control".
Card 1 title: "Customers, lenders, investors"; explanation on three lines: "Customers pay for what they buy" / "Lenders must be repaid" / "Investors hope for a gain". Small line-drawn ledger-and-coins symbol at the left.
Card 2 title: "Funding and control"; explanation on two lines: "Who receives money" / "and approves spending". Small line-drawn approval-stamp symbol at the left.

Stage label 2: "Interpret value and returns".
Card 3 title: "Valuation"; explanation on two lines: "Estimating what" / "a business is worth". Small line-drawn magnifying glass over a small building.
Card 4 title: "Investor returns"; explanation on two lines: "Gains or losses" / "on invested money". Small line-drawn symbol of three branching arrows, one up, one level, one down.

Stage label 3: "Confirm funding for the work".
Card 5 title: "Funding choices"; explanation on two lines: "Match the money" / "to the work". Small line-drawn two-piece jigsaw symbol.
Card 6 title: "Cash flow"; explanation on two lines: "Money coming in" / "and going out". Small line-drawn calendar with coins symbol.

A short teal downward arrow links each card to the next, and a final arrow leads from card 6 into an ochre banner across the bottom with the exact text on two lines: "Know what can fund" / "a commitment to do the work"; the banner lettering is bold and at least as large as the card titles. Arrows never cross text.

Exactly six cards; every title appears once; reproduce the supplied words with exact spelling and add no other words. Symbols must contain no digits, letters, currency signs or percent signs. No photographs, people, 3D, screens, watermarks, chapter numbers or decorative clutter. Keep all text and arrowheads inside the image.

illustrations.visual_goal: Show nine chapters in three connected moves: choose and justify work; assess and change delivery; apply the common method to four operating choices.
illustrations.layout:
Heading: "COMMIT".
Exactly NINE chapter cards organized into THREE clearly separated horizontal bands, stacked from top to bottom. This is a compact overview, not a tall poster.

First band label: "Choose and justify the work".
Two chapter cards across the band, with an arrow between them:
"Set priorities" / "Fit the cash and team time"
"Test revenue assumptions" / "Does the change bring sales?"

A centered downward arrow connects the first band to the second.
Second band label: "Assess and change how work is delivered".
Three chapter cards across the band, with arrows left to right:
"Assess capability" / "What can the team support?"
"Trace the work" / "Fix roles before hiring"
"Plan for growth" / "Choose and pay for system changes"

A centered downward arrow connects the second band to the third.
Third band label: "Apply the same reasoning to four choices".
Four chapter cards in a clearly balanced TWO-BY-TWO grid within this band. Top-left "Cloud costs" / "Rented computing per customer task"; top-right "Resilience" / "Restore service after failure"; bottom-left "AI strategy" / "Artificial intelligence: sell it, use it, or be replaced by it?"; bottom-right "Acquisitions and separations" / "Buying or splitting off a business".
These four application cards have NO arrows between them: they are different applications of the shared method, not sequential prerequisites. Use a single branch or bracket to show that the same reasoning reaches all four.

Inside the third band, below the four cards, one small single-line key in plain lettering: "Artificial intelligence (AI): software that predicts or generates content from data".
An arrow from the third band reaches one gold bottom banner: "Fund feasible work and review the evidence".
Only the listed nine chapter cards; no extra or duplicated card. Do not number chapters or suggest that cloud changes must precede resilience, AI or acquisitions.
illustrations.alt: Nine chapters in three moves under the heading COMMIT. First, choose and justify the work: set priorities to fit cash and team time, then test whether the change brings sales. Second, assess and change how work is delivered: find what the team can support, fix roles and decisions before hiring, then choose and pay for system changes. Third, apply the same reasoning to four separate choices: cloud costs as rented computing per customer task, resilience as restoring service after failure, artificial intelligence (software that predicts or generates content from data) as three questions, sell it, use it or be replaced by it, and buying or splitting off a business. All lead to one outcome: fund feasible work and review the evidence.
illustrations.caption: Five chapters establish what deserves money and what delivery requires; four apply that reasoning independently.
illustrations.placement: immediately after the heading The Learning Path, before the existing linked chapter walkthrough

illustrations.visual_goal: Connect working arrangements, the source of help and engagement terms to the adviser and operating partner roles, culminating in useful support with explicit accountability.
illustrations.layout:
Heading: "COLLABORATE".
Exactly FIVE chapter cards in a coherent two-level framework, flowing downward to a gold purpose banner.
Top level has three chapter cards across, connected left to right:
"Plan investor support" / "Match the arrangement to priorities" (small paired organization blocks)
"Choose the right help" / "Compare sources for the gap" (small choice or search symbol)
"Set the terms of help" / "Agree work, authority and handover" (small agreement sheet)

The top sequence leads into a second level with two larger cards side by side, grouped under the exact label "Understand the people behind the help":
"Clarify the adviser's role" / "Assignment and reporting relationship" (small single specialist symbol)
"Technology operating partners" / "Wider support for the company" (small connected capability nodes)
Treat these two as complementary lenses, without implying that an adviser must become an operating partner, or that every company needs both. Show a branch from the agreed-support framework to both role cards. No arrow from one role card to the other.

Both role cards connect to the single ochre bottom purpose banner. Banner exact text: "Useful support with accountability, cost and dependence understood".
The visual should read as overall arrangement, chosen help, agreed engagement, then the people and function supporting it. No investor superiority claim and no assumed mandatory investor intervention.
illustrations.alt: The working arrangement leads to a choice of help and agreed engagement terms. The adviser and technology operating partner chapters clarify the people and wider function behind that help. Together they support useful collaboration with accountability, cost and dependence understood.
illustrations.caption: The working arrangement shapes the help you seek and the terms you agree. The last two chapters clarify the individual adviser and the wider operating function, so support contributes to a company plan with clear accountability.
illustrations.placement: immediately after the heading The Learning Path, before the existing linked chapter walkthrough

illustrations.visual_goal: Keep the evidence-carrying onboarding scenario separate from the delayed-financing scenario and its conditional reduction, while connecting both to leadership through change.
illustrations.layout:
Heading: "LEAD". One stacked column, five cards, one per row, read top to bottom, explanation lines at title size.
Group label 1: "Follow a customer setup problem" / "Some setups depend on one specialist" (two lines).
"Use diligence" / "Check the business" / "before the deal is signed"
"Plan the first hundred days" / "Fund the work" / "and review the finding"
"Manage the handover" / "Pass on the evidence" / "and unfinished promises"
Solid teal arrows link cards 1-2 and 2-3; no edge rail. A fine ochre rule separates the groups; no arrow crosses it.
Group label 2: "Separate funding-delay scenario".
"Manage funding delays" / "Expected money is late:" / "replan payments and promised work"
The only connector to card 5 is a dashed navy arrow labelled EXACTLY "Only if a cut is required".
"Plan layoffs" / "Decide what work stops," / "then who leaves"
Teal arrow into the ochre banner: "Account for decisions, evidence" / "and promises through change". Canvas 9:16, paper margins cropped with Pillow (20 px).
illustrations.alt: Five chapters stacked in one column under the heading LEAD. Group one, Follow a customer setup problem, where some setups depend on one specialist: Use diligence (check the business before the deal is signed) leads to Plan the first hundred days (fund the work and review the finding), which leads to Manage the handover (pass on the evidence and unfinished promises). Group two, Separate funding-delay scenario: Manage funding delays (expected money is late: replan payments and promised work) is joined to Plan layoffs (decide what work stops, then who leaves) by a dashed arrow labelled Only if a cut is required. A final banner reads Account for decisions, evidence and promises through change.
illustrations.caption: Three chapters follow the onboarding finding from diligence to handover. Two follow a separate funding delay, which leads to layoffs only if a cut is required.
illustrations.placement: immediately after the heading The Learning Path, before the existing linked chapter walkthrough

illustrations.prompt:
Create ONE finished editorial framework illustration for the introduction to a part of OWNED: Product & Engineering Leadership Under Investors. It maps five chapters, their reading connections and their shared purpose; it is not a business scene. Tall portrait 9:16 composition. Match the book's visual language: warm ivory paper, dark navy text, clean slightly organic ink outlines, pale muted teal cards, soft ochre highlights, restrained flat fills, extremely subtle paper texture.

LAYOUT, STRICT: a single vertical column. Every chapter card spans almost the full image width (side margins no wider than one twentieth of the image), one card per row, read top to bottom. Never place two cards side by side. The image will be shown on a narrow phone screen, so all lettering must be very large: each card title is bold and about one eighteenth of the image width in cap height, and every explanation line is set at EXACTLY the same size as the title, in regular weight, wrapped onto short lines of at most four words so it never shrinks (card 3's explanation therefore runs onto three lines). Fill the column; do not leave empty paper above or below the drawing. No frame, border or ruled lines around the composition.

Heading at the top: "LEARN".
Small group label under the heading: "Four independent case chapters".

Card 1 title: "Hilton and Skype"; explanation: "Explain the investors' successful sale". Small line-drawn open book at the left of the card.
Card 2 title: "Visma"; explanation: "Which investors paid, and which received money?" Small line-drawn magnifying glass at the left of the card.
Card 3 title: "Toys R Us"; explanation: "Why did profit before borrowing costs and tax generate almost no cash?" Small line-drawn stack of coins at the left of the card.
Card 4 title: "TeamSystem"; explanation: "What commitments pass to each new owner?" Small line-drawn chain link at the left of the card.
There are NO arrows between these four cards: the histories do not cause one another. Instead, one fine navy bracket runs down the right margin beside all four cards and turns inward beneath card 4 into a single downward arrow.

That arrow points to one unboxed reading-method line in bold navy lettering, the same size as the card titles, written on three short lines: "What happened", "What might explain it", "What a leader could change", with a small navy arrow between the lines.

A short teal downward arrow leads from the method to card 5, which is slightly taller and is the only card with a soft ochre edge. Card 5 title: "Success for whom, and for how long?"; explanation: "Who gained, who paid, what can the company still do?" Small line-drawn balance scale at the left of the card.

A short teal downward arrow leads from card 5 into an ochre banner across the bottom with the exact text: "Make judgments the evidence supports". Arrows never cross text.

Exactly five cards, one bracket, one method line and one banner; every label appears once; reproduce the supplied labels with exact spelling and add no other words. Symbols must contain no digits, letters, currency signs or percent signs, and no corporate logos. No photographs, people, 3D, screens, watermarks, chapter numbers or decorative clutter. Keep all text and arrowheads inside the image. This is a learning framework, not an investment promise.
illustrations.visual_review: Inspected the installed JPEG (third render; the first two reproduced every label but set the explanation lines at about 13–14 CSS px): five cards one per row, every label reproduced with exact spelling, Toys R Us card asks "Why did profit before borrowing costs and tax generate almost no cash?" on three lines, no arrows between the four case cards, right-margin bracket into the three-line method, ochre-edged closing card and banner; explanation lines 15–16 CSS px at a 327 px phone width (Pillow row measurement).
